key_insight: The paper proposes an expert-in-the-loop, self-evolving annotation framework that uses LLM assistance plus DSM-5-TR alignment to make depression symptom labels more explainable and auditable.
clinical_relevance: It aims to improve the quality of depression research datasets by linking labels to symptom-level evidence and structured criteria, supporting more transparent downstream mental health NLP systems.
method: Selects candidate evidence from text records
Performs criterion-level DSM-5-TR analysis and case-level synthesis
Uses Example Memory and Reflection Memory to incorporate expert feedback without retraining
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a pilot study with expert-reviewed samples, suggesting improved annotation consistency and explainability with less manual revision effort.
watch_item: The framework is presented as a dataset annotation tool rather than a diagnostic system, and its performance across multiple feedback cycles is not yet fully evaluated.
paper_title: Self-Evolving Human-Centered Framework for Explainable Depression Symptom Annotation
